**Converge** is an American [metallic hardcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metalcore "Metalcore")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-2) band formed by vocalist and artist [Jacob Bannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Bannon "Jacob Bannon") and guitarist and producer [Kurt Ballou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Ballou "Kurt Ballou") in [Salem, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salem,_Massachusetts "Salem, Massachusetts"), in 1990.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-BBC_AWLWLB2223-4) While recording their landmark fourth album _[Jane Doe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane\_Doe\_(album) "Jane Doe (album)")_ in 2001, the group became a four-piece with the departure of guitarist [Aaron Dalbec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Dalbec "Aaron Dalbec") and the addition of bassist [Nate Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nate_Newton_(musician) "Nate Newton (musician)") and drummer [Ben Koller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Koller "Ben Koller"). This lineup has remained intact since. The members have also been involved in various side-projects and collaborations, including the bands [Supermachiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supermachiner "Supermachiner") (Bannon), [Old Man Gloom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Man_Gloom "Old Man Gloom") (Newton), and [Mutoid Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutoid_Man "Mutoid Man") (Koller). With their extremely aggressive and boundary-pushing sound, rooted in hardcore and [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music"), they are pioneers of [metalcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metalcore "Metalcore") and its subgenre [mathcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathcore "Mathcore").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:2-5)

Converge rose to prominence with _Jane Doe_, which was ranked the best album of 2001 by [_Terrorizer_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrorizer_(magazine) "Terrorizer (magazine)"), the best album of the decade by Sputnikmusic, and later the 61st-best metal album of all time by _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-7) After, they moved from [Equal Vision Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equal_Vision_Records "Equal Vision Records") to the larger label [Epitaph Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epitaph_Records "Epitaph Records"), and their record production became more elaborate and expensive. Special releases are often handled by [Deathwish Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deathwish_Inc. "Deathwish Inc."), established by Bannon in 1999. Their latest releases are their first full-length collaboration, _[Bloodmoon: I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloodmoon:\_I "Bloodmoon: I")_ (2021) with [Chelsea Wolfe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Wolfe "Chelsea Wolfe") and their eleventh studio album, _[Love Is Not Enough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Is\_Not\_Enough\_(Converge\_album) "Love Is Not Enough (Converge album)")_ (2026). Their twelfth album _[Hum of Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hum\_of\_Hurt "Hum of Hurt")_ was released on June 5, 2026. According to [AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic "AllMusic"), they are "regarded as one of the most original and innovative bands to emerge from the [punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") underground".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:2-5)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Early years and _Halo in a Haystack_ (1990–1994)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years and Halo in a Haystack (1990–1994)")]

Converge was formed in the winter of 1990 by Bannon and Ballou, they were later joined by high school friends Jeff Feinberg and Damon Bellorado in 1991.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:04-8) They started by playing covers of [hardcore punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore_punk "Hardcore punk"), [punk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") and [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") songs. The band soon graduated to playing live performances in mid-1991, after recording some demos on a [4-track recorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multitrack_recording "Multitrack recording"). The band started writing and playing what they consider "relevant" music in 1994.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:04-8)

In 1994 the band became a five-piece when Aaron Dalbec was recruited as a second guitarist. Later in the year Converge released their debut album, _[Halo in a Haystack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halo\_in\_a\_Haystack "Halo in a Haystack")_, released through Earthmaker Records. This was only released as a vinyl record, limited to 1000 copies and it was never repressed.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-9) The record was funded by Bannon through money he saved up from working at a [nursing home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nursing_home "Nursing home").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-10)

### _Petitioning the Empty Sky_, _When Forever Comes Crashing_ and line-up changes (1995–1999)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Petitioning the Empty Sky, When Forever Comes Crashing and line-up changes (1995–1999)")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/Converge_f3596455.jpg/250px-Converge_f3596455.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Converge_f3596455.jpg)

[Kurt Ballou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Ballou "Kurt Ballou") in 2007

In 1995 Converge released their first [compilation album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compilation_album "Compilation album"), _[Caring and Killing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caring\_and\_Killing "Caring and Killing")_, which featured tracks from the band's early work from the years 1991 to 1994. The album was originally released as a European exclusive through Lost & Found Records.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-archived_discog223222-11) However, Converge became dissatisfied with the way the label was handling the release and overcharging fans for their hard-to-find older songs. The album was re-released through [Hydra Head Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydra_Head_Records "Hydra Head Records") on November 17, 1997, in America to "make an overpriced release obsolete".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-liner_notes222-12) Converge also released a seven-inch EP called _Unloved and Weeded Out_ in 1995, which Bannon links more to contemporary Converge than the stuff that predated it.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-13)

In 1996 Converge released a four-song [EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play"), _[Petitioning the Empty Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petitioning\_the\_Empty\_Sky "Petitioning the Empty Sky")._ It was released through [Ferret Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferret_Music "Ferret Music"), and was one of the earliest releases through the newly formed label. Later that same year the record was re-released with four additional new tracks. Two years later, the record was reissued through Converge's new label [Equal Vision Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equal_Vision_Records "Equal Vision Records") on January 20, 1998. This version contained the previous eight tracks as well as three newly added live tracks, recorded during a radio broadcast. Due to the addition of the new tracks, fans and sources consider this to be Converge's second studio album, while the band considers it a compilation album because it is a collection of songs recorded at different times.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:1223222-14)

In early 1997 the band's original bassist, Feinburg, left the band, and was replaced with [Stephen Brodsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Brodsky "Stephen Brodsky"). Also that year, the band signed to Equal Vision Records.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:223222-15) On December 22, 1997, recording for the band's third studio album _[When Forever Comes Crashing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_Forever\_Comes\_Crashing "When Forever Comes Crashing")_ began at Ballou's [GodCity Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Ballou#God_City_Studio "Kurt Ballou"); it finished on January 3, 1998.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-16) On April 14, 1998, Converge released _When Forever Comes Crashing_ through Equal Vision.

In 1998, Brodsky left the band and was replaced by Newton, who initially joined the band as a part-time member while he was still active in another band, [Jesuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesuit_(band) "Jesuit (band)"). Jesuit later disbanded in 1999, allowing Newton to make Converge his main focus. In early 1999, the original drummer Bellorado left the band and he was quickly replaced with John DiGiorgio.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:022222-17) Converge's only release with DiGiorgio was _[The Poacher Diaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Poacher\_Diaries "The Poacher Diaries")_; Koller joined Converge in late 1999, replacing him.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:022222-17) Ballou selected Koller to temporarily fill in while Converge searched for a more permanent replacement for Bellorado, as he was familiar with his work in previous bands, Force Fed Glass and Blue/Green Heart, a band that Ballou and Koller played in together.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-19) After working well with the band during some local shows in Boston, Converge made him an official member.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:12222222-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-21) Newton and Koller remain in the band to this day.

### _Jane Doe_ (2000–2003)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Jane Doe (2000–2003)")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Converge_%40_Roadburn_Festival_2018-04-19_004.jpg/250px-Converge_%40_Roadburn_Festival_2018-04-19_004.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Converge_@_Roadburn_Festival_2018-04-19_004.jpg)

[Jacob Bannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Bannon "Jacob Bannon") performing in 2018

The band was reported to take part in a [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica "Metallica") tribute split series titled _[Crush 'Em All](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crush\_'Em\_All\_Vol.\_1 "Crush 'Em All Vol. 1")_ with [Today Is the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today_Is_the_Day "Today Is the Day") for [Undecided Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undecided_Records "Undecided Records") in 2000 but the release fell through.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:7-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:6-23) In mid-2000 Converge self-released a three-track demo record titled _Jane Doe Demos_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-archived_discog223222-11) This was released on tour and was limited to 100 copies.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] It contained unreleased demo versions of "Bitter & Then Some" and "Thaw" from their upcoming album _[Jane Doe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane\_Doe\_(album) "Jane Doe (album)")_. Converge entered the studio to begin recording in the summer of 2001.

On September 4, 2001, Converge released their fourth studio album, _Jane Doe_. It was met with immediate critical acclaim, with critics praising its poetic lyrics, dynamic range, ferocity and production.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-26) The album was a commercial success in comparison to Converge's previous outings, and both the band and the album have developed a cult following since its release.

It is the band's first studio album to feature Newton and Koller, and the last to feature Dalbec, who was asked to leave the band due to his devotion to his side project [Bane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bane_(band) "Bane (band)").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-27) Converge's first tour in support of _Jane Doe_ was in September 2001 with [Drowningman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drowningman "Drowningman") and Playing Enemy,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-28) however Drowningman later dropped out of the tour to work on a new album.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-29)

In 2002 a music video was released for the track/tracks "Concubine/Fault and Fracture" from the album _Jane Doe_; the music video was directed by Zach Merck.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:223222-15)

On January 28, 2003, Converge released their second compilation album, _[Unloved and Weeded Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unloved\_and\_Weeded\_Out "Unloved and Weeded Out")_. The album was originally released as a three track EP in 1995.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:1223222-14) The 2003 album version contains all three tracks from the 1995 EP but in total features 14 tracks, some of which were previously released rarities while others were previously unreleased.

On February 25, 2003, Converge released their first official [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD"), _The Long Road Home_. It is modeled after band home videos such as [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica "Metallica")'s _[Cliff 'Em All](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cliff\_'Em\_All "Cliff 'Em All")_.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:02222222-30)[Deathwish Inc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deathwish_Inc. "Deathwish Inc.") describes the DVD as a "two disc collection that is as energetic and exciting as the moments the release captures".[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:02222222-30) The DVD also comes with a bonus disk that included three full live sets from the band.

### _You Fail Me_ and _No Heroes_ (2004–2007)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: You Fail Me and No Heroes (2004–2007)")]

In early 2004 the band announced that they were signing to Epitaph Records, having previously been signed to Equal Vision. Bannon stated, "We are confident as artists and genuinely happy about the move. We are part of a diverse, quality roster with Epitaph, rich in both history and integrity. We've struggled for years looking for a supportive label to call home and after a decade we have found it."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-31)

Converge began writing for _[You Fail Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Fail\_Me "You Fail Me")_ after they recorded _Jane Doe_; they wrote on the road during sound checks of shows.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:22222222-32) Converge entered the studio to begin recording in March 2004 mainly at GodCity Studio. On September 20, 2004, Converge released their fifth studio album, _You Fail Me_. It was the band's first to chart commercially, reaching number 171 on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:1542-33)

On February 14, 2005, a music video was released for the track "Eagles Become Vultures", directed by Zach Merck.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-34) Converge's first tour in support of _You Fail Me_ started in September 2004 with [Cave In](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cave_In "Cave In") and [Between the Buried and Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Between_the_Buried_and_Me "Between the Buried and Me").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-35)

In 2005 Equal Vision reissued _Petitioning the Empty Sky_ and _When Forever Comes Crashing_. These reissues gave the albums one new bonus track each; _Petitioning the Empty Sky_ received an alternate version of the song "Love as Arson" and _When Forever Comes Crashing_ received a demo version of the song "Bitter and Then Some". These reissues also came with new album artwork by [Aaron Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Turner "Aaron Turner") of [Isis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isis_(band) "Isis (band)"). Ballou said in an interview that he wanted to remix and remaster the albums because the quality of Converge's recordings had improved so much that the original recordings were "becoming distracting".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-36) These reissues became the standard versions of these albums.

In early July 2006 Converge's official website announced the title of their upcoming album, _[No Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No\_Heroes "No Heroes")_, as well as the meaning behind it: "These days, cowards outnumber the heroes, and the begging souls outweigh the calloused hands of the hardest of workers. Both in life and in art, the lack of passion is sickening, and the lust for complacency is poisonous. This album is the artistic antithesis of that sinking world; a thorn in the side of their beast. It's for those who move mountains one day at a time. It's for those who truly understand sacrifice. In our world of enemies, we will walk alone...".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-37)

On October 24, 2006, Converge released their sixth studio album, _No Heroes_. This was the first Converge album to be self-produced by Ballou with no input from other producers, at his own GodCity Studio.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-38)

The same day as the album's release, Converge released a music video for the title track, directed by Ryan Zunkley.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-39)

Converge's first tour in support of _No Heroes_ started in November 2006 with [Some Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some_Girls_(California_band) "Some Girls (California band)"), [Modern Life Is War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Life_Is_War "Modern Life Is War"), [Blacklisted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blacklisted_(band) "Blacklisted (band)"), [Kylesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylesa "Kylesa") and [Gospel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_(hardcore_punk_band) "Gospel (hardcore punk band)").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-40) Despite their growing prominence, Converge continued to appear at small independent events such as [Fluff Fest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluff_Fest "Fluff Fest") in the Czech Republic, which they played in 2007.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-marast2007-41)

### _Axe to Fall_ (2008–2011)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Axe to Fall (2008–2011)")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Converge_f4098903.jpg/250px-Converge_f4098903.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Converge_f4098903.jpg)

[Nate Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nate_Newton_(musician) "Nate Newton (musician)") in 2007

In November 2008 Converge began writing _[Axe to Fall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axe\_to\_Fall "Axe to Fall")_. Following a short tour in March 2009 with [Ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremony_(punk_band) "Ceremony (punk band)"), [Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coliseum_(band) "Coliseum (band)"), [Pulling Teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulling_Teeth_(band) "Pulling Teeth (band)") and [Rise and Fall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rise_and_Fall_(band) "Rise and Fall (band)"), Converge entered the studio to begin recording in May 2009. During this short tour, the band debuted a few new songs live, and footage could be seen online.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-42)

The album was produced by Ballou, at GodCity Studio. In August 2009, two months prior to the release of _Axe to Fall_, Converge made the opening track, "Dark Horse", available for [streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media") and as a free download. It was noted for being one of the few tracks lacking guest musicians, and was met with a very positive reaction from reviewers. The title track was also made available for free download in September 2009. The entire album was available for streaming on Converge's [MySpace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MySpace "MySpace") page one week before the official release date. On October 14, 2009, a music video was released for the title track of the album, directed by Craig Murray.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-43)

On October 20, 2009, Converge released their seventh studio album, _Axe to Fall_. On November 7, the "Axe to Fall" video debuted on [MTV2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV2 "MTV2")'s heavy metal music program, _[Headbangers Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headbangers\_Ball "Headbangers Ball")_.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-44)

Converge's first tour in support of _Axe to Fall_ was the [Metalocalypse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metalocalypse "Metalocalypse") tour in late 2009, sponsored by [Cartoon Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartoon_Network "Cartoon Network")'s [Adult Swim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Swim "Adult Swim"). Alongside [High on Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_on_Fire "High on Fire"), Converge held an opening slot for co-headliners [Mastodon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastodon_(band) "Mastodon (band)") and [Dethklok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dethklok "Dethklok").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-45) Converge's first headlining tour in support of the album started in April 2010 with [Coalesce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coalesce_(band) "Coalesce (band)"), [Harvey Milk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Milk_(band) "Harvey Milk (band)"), [Gaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_(band) "Gaza (band)"), Lewd Acts and Black Breath. Converge began the European part of their world tour in July 2010 with [Kylesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylesa "Kylesa"), Gaza and [Kvelertak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kvelertak "Kvelertak").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-46)

In July 2010 the band released a limited-edition 7-inch vinyl single, _[On My Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On\_My\_Shield "On My Shield")_. It was released in three different colors, with each limited to 1,000 copies. One version was sold during Converge's 2010 European tours, one was sold through the band's Epitaph web store, and the final version was distributed to various vinyl retailers.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-48)

### _All We Love We Leave Behind_ (2012–2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: All We Love We Leave Behind (2012–2016)")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Converge_%40_Roadburn_Festival_2018-04-19_002.jpg/250px-Converge_%40_Roadburn_Festival_2018-04-19_002.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Converge_@_Roadburn_Festival_2018-04-19_002.jpg)

[Ben Koller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Koller "Ben Koller") in 2018

In January 2012 Converge completed writing for their eighth studio album, _[All We Love We Leave Behind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_We\_Love\_We\_Leave\_Behind "All We Love We Leave Behind")_.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-50) The following day, Ballou announced plans via his [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") page to begin recording with the band in January. On August 28, 2012, a music video was released for the track "Aimless Arrow" from the upcoming album, directed by Max Moore.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-52) On the same day, Converge revealed the album's artwork, depicting a lunar cycle. On October 3, 2012, the album was available to stream in its entirety on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), a week before its official release.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-53)

On October 9, 2012, Converge released their eighth studio album, _All We Love We Leave Behind._ It peaked at number 70 on the _Billboard_ 200,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:1542-33) surpassing _Axe to Fall_ in terms of commercial success. Converge's first headlining tour in support of _All We Love We Leave Behind_ started in October 2012 with [Torche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torche_(band) "Torche (band)"), [Kvelertak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kvelertak "Kvelertak"), [Nails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nails_(band) "Nails (band)") and Whips/Chains.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-54)

On April 17, 2014, another music video was released for the track "Precipice / All We Love We Leave Behind", directed by Craig Murray.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-55)

On October 15, 2015, Deathwish's YouTube channel released a trailer for Converge's [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") set, _[Thousands of Miles Between Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thousands\_of\_Miles\_Between\_Us\_(album) "Thousands of Miles Between Us (album)")_. This was released on November 27, 2015.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-56) The set was described by Deathwish as the long-awaited sequel to their landmark 2003 DVD release, _The Long Road Home_. The footage includes a full 20-song Converge set and over 15 hours of live, rare, and previously unseen footage, which is claimed to span over a decade in the life of the band.

On April 29, 2016, Converge announced plans to reissue the album _You Fail Me_ (12 years after the original release); it was made available for pre-order the same day.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-57) On May 2, 2016 the title track from the upcoming version of the album was made available to stream on [SoundCloud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoundCloud "SoundCloud").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-58) On June 17, 2016, Converge reissued the album under the name _[You Fail Me Redux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Fail\_Me\_Redux "You Fail Me Redux")_ through Epitaph and Deathwish. Ballou remixed the album and Alan Douches remastered it. The album was also repackaged by Bannon. Ballou explained in an interview with [Noisey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noisey "Noisey") that after he recorded and mixed the album _No Heroes_, he wanted to go back and remix _You Fail Me,_ because he and the rest of the band were "never quite content with the original mix".[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:1322-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-60)

### _The Dusk In Us_ and _Beautiful Ruin_ (2017–2020)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: The Dusk In Us and Beautiful Ruin (2017–2020)")]

On January 16, 2017, the band announced they would release a live album of their _Jane Doe_ set from the Netherlands Roadburn Festival in 2016, titled _[Jane Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane\_Doe\_(album)#Jane\_Live "Jane Doe (album)")_.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-61) The album was put up for pre-order the same day. Deathwish's SoundCloud put the live version of the track "Jane Doe" up for streaming. _Jane Live_ was released on March 3, 2017.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-62)

Koller announced during an interview that the band was planning to start tracking for a new album in the spring of 2017.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-63) Following their tour on April 8, Converge planned to promptly head into the studio to record their next album.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-64) On May 27, 2017, [DigBoston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DigBoston "DigBoston") published an interview with the band's vocalist Jacob Bannon, who revealed that the band had 18 songs already written. He stated the album is "very powerful" and will be a "progression of something [they] did previously."[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-65)

On July 25, 2017, Converge released the single "[I Can Tell You About Pain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_Tell_You_About_Pain "I Can Tell You About Pain")", accompanied by a video directed by Tony Wolski. The single also contained the non-album track “Eve” as a b-side.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-66)

On August 15, Converge released the new track "Under Duress", available for streaming. It was described by Bannon as his "emotional reaction to the complex world in which we live". With the announcement of the song, the album's tracklist and cover art were revealed.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:12-67) The band toured in Europe in August 2017 prior to the release.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:12-67)

The following month another track, “Reptilian”, was made available for streaming.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-68) "A Single Tear" was made available for streaming on October 31, accompanied by a video directed by Max Moore. The video was described by having "heavy with symbolism about parenthood and connection."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-69)_[The Dusk in Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dusk\_in\_Us "The Dusk in Us")_ was released in the through Epitaph and Deathwish on November 3, 2017.

On June 28, 2018, the band uploaded a short series of images to their Instagram page, alluding to a new release.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-70) On June 29, the band released the _[Beautiful Ruin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beautiful\_Ruin "Beautiful Ruin")_ EP via Epitaph and Deathwish, along with a music video for the song "Melancholia", directed by Tony Wolski.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-71) The EP consists of four tracks recorded during the sessions for _The Dusk in Us_ which did not make the cut.

Under the name Shattered Void, Converge contributed the new song "I Won't Let You Go" to the soundtrack for _[Cyberpunk 2077](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk\_2077#Music "Cyberpunk 2077")_, a 2020 video game.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-stereogum-11.18.20-1)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Artistry")]

### Musical style and influences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Musical style and influences")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Converge_009.jpg/250px-Converge_009.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Converge_009.jpg)

Converge performing in 2008

Converge's music has been described as "bleak and [dissonant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consonance_and_dissonance "Consonance and dissonance")."[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-80) The band's style is rooted in both [hardcore punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore_punk "Hardcore punk") and [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music")[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-Tiny2222-81) and they are considered one of the earliest and most influential [metalcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metalcore "Metalcore") bands.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-Caring2222-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-BBC_AWLWLB2222-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-84) Their sound has also been categorized as [mathcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathcore "Mathcore"),[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-Tiny2222-81)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-Bio2222-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-Sum_of_the_Score2222-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-See_page_12,_to_the_bottom_right2222-88)[post-hardcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-hardcore "Post-hardcore"),[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:32-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-collide2-90)[noisecore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noisecore "Noisecore"),[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-ksp22-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:22-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-93) experimental hardcore,[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-94) or simply hardcore.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:22-92)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-97)

Matt Mills of _[Metal Hammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal\_Hammer "Metal Hammer")_ said that Converge perform a "technical-yet-incensed take on their genre."[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-98)[AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic "AllMusic") describes them as a "revered [punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") metal band that combined the aggression of hardcore and metal with the complexity and [polyrhythms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyrhythm "Polyrhythm") of [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz")."[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:2-5) Their 2001 album _[Jane Doe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane\_Doe\_(album) "Jane Doe (album)")_, which has become their most acclaimed work,[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-99)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-100)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-101) introduced an [experimental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_music "Experimental music") approach and emphasis on rhythmical complexity, which are defining features of mathcore. However, Bannon has stated: "I really don't know what mathcore is. Converge is an aggressive band. We have elements of hardcore, punk, and metal for sure. But I think trying to define our efforts and other bands with a generic [subgenre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subgenre "Subgenre") name is counter productive. We all have something unique to offer and should be celebrated for those qualities rather than having them generalized for easy consumption."[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-102)

Converge started writing and playing what they consider "relevant" music in 1994. At that time they started incorporating influences like [Starkweather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starkweather_(band) "Starkweather (band)"),[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:3-103)[Neurosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurosis_(band) "Neurosis (band)"),[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-104)[the Accüsed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Acc%C3%BCsed "The Accüsed"),[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:3-103)[Rorschach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rorschach_(band) "Rorschach (band)"),[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:3-103)[Born Against](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_Against "Born Against"),[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:3-103)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:4-105)[Moss Icon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moss_Icon "Moss Icon"),[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:4-105)[Universal Order of Armageddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Order_of_Armageddon "Universal Order of Armageddon"),[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:4-105)[Heroin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroin_(band) "Heroin (band)"),[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:4-105) and [Mohinder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohinder_(band) "Mohinder (band)")[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:4-105) into their approach.

In a 2012 interview, Bannon told Jonny Cohn of _[The Aquarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Aquarian\_Weekly "The Aquarian Weekly")_ that the band "don’t really look to any outside influences all that much anymore. We kind of haven’t for a long time. We have been a band for over two decades. We’re more introverted. We’re used to writing and creating in our own little bubble. We love and appreciate all different kinds of music and at times you can hear little subtle things come out but for the most part, they’re just an extension and exploration of things that we’ve done in the past."[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-106)

Kurt Ballou has produced (and co-produced) the majority of Converge's albums at his own GodCity Studio. He has always been involved in the production of Converge's albums, but it was not until their 2006 album, _No Heroes_, that he was involved in the entire recording and mixing process.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:1322-59) This became the standard for Converge releases afterwards. One reason Ballou claimed to get into the studio side of music was to have "maximum control over our music". He stated, "When we were starting out, no one wanted to help us anyway, so if we didn't take control, nothing was going to get done."[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-stylus_mag-107)

### Lyrics and vocal delivery

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Lyrics and vocal delivery")]

Scott Butterworth of Noisey has described Bannon's vocals "as just another sonic element—more percussive and tonal than lyrical—allowing listeners to develop an emotional understanding of the material even without a precise knowledge of the words."[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:0222-108) Sammy O'Hagar of [Metalsucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MetalSucks "MetalSucks") stated Bannon's vocals "[are] as much a part of Converge's uniqueness as is Ballou's nimble riffing".[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:12322-109) According to Joe Davita of Loudwire, "Converge don’t need any clean singing in order to make their mark. At times sounding less like a voice and more like a percussive instrument adding yet another hard-hitting layer to the music, frontman Jacob Bannon’s delivery is a unique and iconic feature of the metalcore genre."[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-110)

### Artwork

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Artwork")]

Bannon has designed all of Converge's artwork since their 1996 release, _Petitioning the Empty Sky_. Although reissues of older albums have had artwork done by Aaron Turner such as the 2005 reissues of _Petitioning the Empty Sky_ and _When Forever Comes Crashing_, Bannon still took part in the design process of these reissues. In an interview with _[Revolver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolver\_(magazine) "Revolver (magazine)")_, Bannon shared his art process, saying, "When I work I usually start out with a sketch of some kind, either in my process book or on a scrap of paper," he explains. "I also did this with the _Jane Doe_ album. By doing that, I work through ideas, write about them, and force them to evolve into something more refined. Process is extremely important for me—it allows me to have a log of my ideas, whether they're successful or not. That said, I sketched the basic cover and started building it in layers, using acrylic, ink, and spray paint. Because of the nature of the work and the need for flexibility in the imagery, I decided to build it in physical layers and scan certain elements for future use."[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:02-111)

Since the release of Converge's 2001 album _Jane Doe_, the cover art of the woman simply known as "Jane" (revealed in October 2021 to be based on a photograph of French actress and model [Audrey Marnay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audrey_Marnay "Audrey Marnay"))[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-113) has become Converge's icon, in a similar vein to [Iron Maiden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Maiden "Iron Maiden")'s [Eddie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_(mascot) "Eddie (mascot)") or [Motörhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mot%C3%B6rhead "Motörhead")'s [Snaggletooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mot%C3%B6rhead#Name_and_logo "Motörhead").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:02-111)

## Collaborations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Collaborations")]

Converge have collaborated with numerous musicians throughout their work such as members of [Cave In](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cave_In "Cave In"), [The Hope Conspiracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hope_Conspiracy "The Hope Conspiracy"), [Genghis Tron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genghis_Tron "Genghis Tron"), [Neurosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurosis_(band) "Neurosis (band)") and [Disfear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disfear "Disfear"). Most of these bands are featured on the band's collaborative album _[Axe to Fall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axe\_to\_Fall "Axe to Fall")_. However, with the exception of _Axe to Fall,_ Converge tend not to include many guests on their albums, and the guests that are included have minor roles such as backing vocals. The band have also worked with [Tomas Lindberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomas_Lindberg "Tomas Lindberg") (of [At the Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At_the_Gates "At the Gates"), [Skitsystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skitsystem "Skitsystem"), The Great Deceiver, and Disfear),[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:1-114)[Aaron Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Turner "Aaron Turner") (of [Isis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isis_(band) "Isis (band)") and [Old Man Gloom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Man_Gloom "Old Man Gloom")),[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:1-114) and [Kevin Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hope_Conspiracy "The Hope Conspiracy") (of [All Pigs Must Die](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Pigs_Must_Die_(band) "All Pigs Must Die (band)") and The Hope Conspiracy),[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:1-114) all of whom provided vocals for a cover of [Entombed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entombed_(band) "Entombed (band)")'s "Wolverine Blues" performed by Converge.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-115)

### With Cave In

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: With Cave In")]

See also: [Cave In](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cave_In "Cave In")

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Cave_In.jpg/250px-Cave_In.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cave_In.jpg)

Cave In performing at the Backstage Club in Munich, 2006

After touring together in 2004, every member of Cave In and Converge entered Ballou's GodCity Studio to lay the foundation for what was intended to become a full-length collaborative album between the two bands. Tentatively dubbed the "Verge-In" sessions (an [amalgamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amalgamation_(names) "Amalgamation (names)") of the bands' names), the project was described as sounding "like this freaky mix of _[Ride the Lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ride\_the\_Lightning "Ride the Lightning")_-era [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica "Metallica") meets [Mars Volta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Volta "Mars Volta") meets the [Allman Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allman_Brothers "Allman Brothers")."[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-noisecreep-vergein22-116) Due to both groups growing busier with their primary bands, as well as creative differences, the project eventually fizzled out.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-noisecreep-vergein22-116)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-117) Brodsky described the sessions as being a "bigger project than anyone had anticipated taking on... The idea was to put out some sort of release at some point. But as with anything that has too many cooks in the kitchen, the project got delayed, and certain people felt one way or another about the pieces we came up with, and in the end, there was a very small portion of material that everyone could agree on."[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-noisecreep-vergein22-116) Tracks from the abandoned Verge-In sessions were reworked and transformed years later into the Converge songs "Plagues" from _No Heroes_ and "Effigy", "Cruel Bloom", and "Wretched World" from _Axe to Fall_, the latter of which were heavily reworked by members of [Genghis Tron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genghis_Tron "Genghis Tron").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-acutabove22-118) Bannon said he believes there are only two unused and half-finished tracks from these sessions that could end up being reworked into new Cave In songs down the road.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-SPBinterview22-119) Brodsky said what became "Effigy" was some of the best material from the sessions and expressed interest in going back and finishing the remaining unreleased tracks at some point.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-noisecreep-vergein22-116)

Cave In and Converge members have collaborated numerous times, Brodsky had been the bassist of Converge from 1997 to 1998. Ballou produced Cave In's first two records, _[Beyond Hypothermia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyond\_Hypothermia\_(album) "Beyond Hypothermia (album)")_ and _[Until Your Heart Stops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Until\_Your\_Heart\_Stops "Until Your Heart Stops")._ Koller became a temporary drummer for Cave In during their support tour of their fourth studio album, _[Perfect Pitch Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfect\_Pitch\_Black "Perfect Pitch Black")_. Cave In also recorded two songs with Koller, "Dead Already" and "Shapeshifter"; these songs were released together on a limited-edition cassette single.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-mtv-sept2005-120) Bands that feature both members of Cave In and Converge include [Kid Kilowatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kid_Kilowatt "Kid Kilowatt"), [Old Man Gloom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Man_Gloom "Old Man Gloom"), [Doomriders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doomriders "Doomriders"), [Mutoid Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutoid_Man "Mutoid Man") and Bannon's [Wear Your Wounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wear_Your_Wounds "Wear Your Wounds") live band.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-121) The relationship between the two bands has been described as "incestuous" by members of each band.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-122)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-123) The bands even went as far to joke with each other about hosting a festival titled "IncestFest", which would only feature bands and side-projects that are related to Cave In and Converge.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-124)

### Blood Moon

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Converge_(band)&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Blood Moon")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/AdamWright-Treefort-2016-ChelseaWolfe-49_%2831415982664%29.jpg/120px-AdamWright-Treefort-2016-ChelseaWolfe-49_%2831415982664%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AdamWright-Treefort-2016-ChelseaWolfe-49_(31415982664).jpg)

Blood Moon collaborator Chelsea Wolfe.

In April 2016, all four members of Converge, and guests [Chelsea Wolfe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Wolfe "Chelsea Wolfe"), Ben Chisholm (also of Chelsea Wolfe), Stephen Brodsky of Cave In and [Steve Von Till](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Von_Till "Steve Von Till") of [Neurosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurosis_(band) "Neurosis (band)"), collaborated for four limited European performances titled Blood Moon. The collective performed "[ambient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambient_music "Ambient music")/[post-rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-rock "Post-rock") interpretations"[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-noisey-bloodmoon232-125) of various tracks from Converge's discography, particularly their "lesser-heard and slower work."[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-nme-bloodmoon22-126)

The first Blood Moon set took place at Postbahnhof in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") on April 11.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:03-127) The second took place at La Cartonnerie in [Reims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reims "Reims") on April 12.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:03-127) The third took place at [Electric Brixton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_Brixton "Electric Brixton") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") on April 13.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:03-127) The fourth and final Blood Moon show took place after a special one-off Converge set where they played their 2001 album _Jane Doe_ in its entirety for the first and presumably last time, to celebrate its 15-year anniversary. This took place at the [Roadburn Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roadburn_Festival "Roadburn Festival") in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") on April 14.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:0-128) The following Blood Moon set took place at Roadburn on April 16.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-:03-127)

In Tom Hartley of [NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")'s review of their London performance, he said: "As one of only four European cities visited by Converge on this tour, it felt truly fortunate to witness such a unique show and once again reaffirmed they are crushingly brilliant with whatever they choose to do."[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-nme-bloodmoon22-126) In Kim Kelly of [Noisey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noisey "Noisey")'s review of Blood Moon's Roadburn Festival performance, she said: "I hadn't realized Converge's Jacob Bannon had such a powerful clean voice, or just how well it would mesh with Chelsea Wolfe's; I stood rooted to the spot for a good half hour if not more, totally sucked in by what was happening onstage. It was obvious that the musicians involved had put a lot of thought into what they were presenting up there."[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converge_(band)#cite_note-noisey-bloodmoon232-125)

These performances paved the way for Converge's 2021 full-length collaboration album with Wolfe, _[Bloodmoon: I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloodmoon:\_I "Bloodmoon: I")_.
